article.statement: For a Coxeter diagram Γ, its Coxeter group W, and J ⊆ Γ₀, the functor F from the universal groupoid with chamber objects (x,I) to BH sends (x,I) to I and the singleton arrow labelled x⁻¹y to the BH arrow with that label. It is a universal groupoid covering with Deck(F) ≅ N(W,J). The introductory statement also requires identification with the wall-crossing groupoid of the Tits cone intersection, generation by adjacent simple wall crossings, and the N(W,J)-quotient description.
article.locator: Theorem 1.3, printed p. 2; Theorem 4.7, printed pp. 16–17; Definition 4.3, printed p. 15; Proposition 4.4, printed p. 16.

portal.statement: The local portal entry establishes the algebraic covering, deck-group and quotient assertions at arbitrary rank. It separately imposes finite rank for identification with geometric relative chambers and adjacent-wall generators; neither W nor W_J is required to be finite.

requested_main_obligations.unresolved: Reconcile the portal's explicit finite-rank geometric convention with the exact requested article formulation. Arbitrary Coxeter type, finite rank, and finite Coxeter group are different conditions; none may be substituted silently.

article.statement: Let Γ be a Coxeter diagram, J ⊆ Γ₀, and I,K associates of J. Any two standard expressions of w ∈ Hom_BH(I,K) are related by a sequence of atomic braid relations. Standard expressions are those of Definition 4.9, and atomic braid relations are those of Definition 4.18, using Lemma 4.15.
article.locator: Theorem 1.4, printed p. 3; Theorem 4.21, printed p. 20; Definition 4.9, printed p. 17; Lemma 4.15 and Definition 4.18, printed p. 19.

portal.statement: For a Coxeter system without restriction on rank or type, any two finite length-additive standard expressions of the same Brink–Howlett morphism are connected by finitely many atomic braid relations. The entry explicitly supplies the finite relative-root condition needed when invoking its two-generator common-prefix result.
